source.baseline_kind: Local read-only content snapshot of installed source. No separate upstream license identified in the snapshot.

runtime.platform: native Linux x86_64 in an isolated alpine:3.22 container
runtime.isolation: Read-only container, loopback only, tmpfs, synthetic credentials and no production or private state.

failed_attempt.outcome: runtime fault in Go net/http routing during the test
failed_attempt.resolution: The same App ELF and worker ZIP completed on native x86_64 without a source change.

observations.evidence: An isolated native App installed the indexed ZIP, served the native form, saved synthetic configuration and rejected an unauthenticated test call.
The loopback peer received the tenant token request and an interactive test card for the configured chat. The page showed the resulting message ID once.
The wrong token returned 403. The anonymous signed-route boundary accepted a source-exempt card event, ran the real parser and plugin MessageAction, and sent the reply to the original message ID.
The started host used its ordinary notification path and the isolated provider received the title at the configured chat.

open_in_scope.remaining: Standard /sites session, list/card actions and pending Cookie text use the ordinary site APIs. The current inbound branch dispatches installed plugin commands and [PLUGIN] callbacks.
Standard /subscribes sessions, callbacks and follow-up edits must connect to native subscription operations.
Native media/resource list producers, pending selection, downloads, and reply editing must use existing host search and download paths. Worker module declarations alone are insufficient.
Ordinary transfer failure retry button and actual completion feedback need host integration using stable native history IDs.

Remaining distinct checks include administrator text command and processing reaction, cryptographic webhooks, file/voice/image upload, disabled fetch_chats, browser operation and clone or reload boundaries.

Compare ordinary known notification/reaction failure handling against the source internal logging and fallback returns. Current SDK may emit an additional module error event. Fetch chats has a generic provider rejection where the source exposes an API code. Preserve the opaque-write fence and redact provider response secrets.

excluded: AI direct tool/module and AI-only inbound attachment download
AI notification preference sync and multiuser account mapping
AI transfer recovery and agent callbacks
adaptations: The standard scoped message.receive entry replaces self-HTTP with the host API token. The actual raw anonymous Lark webhook and exact Lark source bind the grant.
The fixed international Lark origin is selected by the host at init. A private loopback-only field exists for the isolated test App.
Local outgoing attachments use rooted identity grants and a 30 MiB worker limit. Public image reads use the host network grant. No production API credentials are present in this record.
Known opaque provider write failures fence further writes in that same invocation. Source reuse and source-license identification are recorded in ORIGIN.json.
release: Local commits only. Candidate ZIP is outside the release build registry while acceptance is open.

candidate_after_review.kind: focused Go worker test with a synthetic loopback provider, not a new full native run
observations: The real worker HTTP method returned success after one failed direct reply to the original test-card message. A generic error was logged and no second outbound write occurred.
Without a client, bare test_ok fell through to ordinary forwarding. A forwarding error was logged without changing the webhook acknowledgement.
candidate_after_review.independent_source_review: /root/emby compared actual test_ok against fixed source and identified the direct reply error regression. The previously executed native test covered only the distinct [PLUGIN]… callback path.
